Crisis Period Identification

Crisis periods are defined as days when 60-day annualized volatility exceeds the 90th percentile (24.4%).

Crisis Days Identified: 634 days across the dataset. These periods typically coincide with:
  • 2008-2009 Global Financial Crisis
  • 2011 US credit rating downgrade
  • 2020 COVID-19 pandemic volatility
  • 2022 rate hike shock environment

Statistical Methodology

Seasonal significance is assessed using a two-tailed t-test on daily log returns. Returns with p-value < 0.05 are considered statistically significant. Note that monthly sample sizes vary and early data (pre-2003) may have unreliable volume.

  • -3.10%

Tail Risk Assessment: The excess kurtosis of 7.02 indicates that gold returns have fatter tails than a normal distribution. This means extreme moves (both up and down) occur more frequently than would be expected under Gaussian assumptions. The negative skew (-0.47) indicates that large negative returns are more extreme than large positive ones.

6. Key Takeaways & Forward-Looking Considerations

Summary Statistics

  • Total Return: 1863.2% over 25.5 years
  • Risk-Adjusted Performance: Sharpe-like ratio of 0.70
  • Worst Case: -48.4% maximum drawdown
  • Tail Risk: 1% VaR at -3.10% daily loss

Volatility Regime Insights

  • Low Vol Period: 13.5% annualized threshold – gold spends 33% of time in this regime, typically during stable macroeconomic conditions.
  • High Vol Period: 17.2% annualized threshold – 634 crisis days identified, predominantly during systemic stress events.
  • Current Regime: Last observed volatility at 37.2% (annualized), currently classified as high.

Seasonal Considerations

  • Best Month: Jan (0.14% annualized)
  • Worst Month: Jun (-0.03% annualized)
  • Note: Month-to-month variation is relatively modest and most differences are not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

Risk Management Implications

Position Sizing Guidance

  • 95% VaR suggests daily loss risk of -1.76%
  • For 2% daily risk limit, consider 1.1x leverage cap

Volatility Adjustment

  • In high-vol regimes, reduce position size by ~-1%
  • Crisis periods may warrant 38% vol increase

Forward-Looking Scenarios

  • Bullish Scenario: Continued macroeconomic uncertainty, central bank buying, and inflation concerns could sustain elevated gold prices.
  • Bearish Scenario: Sustained real rate increases, dollar strength, and risk-on sentiment could pressure gold lower.
  • Volatility Outlook: With current vol at 37.2%, we're in a high volatility regime. Historical precedent suggests staying defensive if vol continues rising.
